captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a road bike's front steering assembly, featuring a dark blue head tube, a black carbon fork crown with two thin black blades, and a light grey alloy stem. Curved drop handlebars in light grey are clamped to the stem, complete with black brake hoods and bar tape grips. The steering column (steerer tube) is inside the head tube, rotating via a revolute joint to steer the fork and handlebars relative to the frame.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a road bike front fork and handlebar assembly. It should include a dark blue head tube, a black carbon fork with two blades, a light grey alloy stem, and curved drop handlebars with black brake hoods and grips, featuring a revolute joint allowing the fork and handlebars to steer together.
captions.factory: Construct the assembly by first modeling the head tube as a cylinder. Build the steering column (steerer) using a cylinder that passes through the head tube, and attach the fork crown and blades (using box/extruded shapes) to its lower end. On the upper end of the steerer, construct the alloy stem using box primitives, and sweep or loft a circular profile along a curved path to form the drop handlebars. Add black boxes or cylinders for the brake hoods and grips, and define a revolute joint between the head tube and the steerer/handlebar sub-assembly.
